_readme: Logical, information and error-handling function fixtures.
`expected` is always the value Excel or Google Sheets produces.
Arity cases use `source: "google-sheets"`. Excel refuses the formula entry
outright, so it has no cell result to record; Google Sheets accepts it and
evaluates to #N/A with a 'Wrong number of arguments' message. That #N/A is
the only observable spreadsheet answer, so every arity fixture expects it.
Two cross-cutting engine defects show up repeatedly below and are worth
* arguments are evaluated eagerly and errors are ordinary strings, so an
error in a branch that is not taken can still surface, and any string
that starts with '#' is mistaken for an error;
* comparison operators coerce both sides with toNum, which turns an error
into 0, so an error inside a comparison is erased before IFERROR or the
IS* family can ever see it.

cases.notes: Minimum arity is two; the omitted value_if_false defaults to FALSE.
A numeric condition is false only at exactly 0.
Text is not a logical value; Excel rejects it. The engine uses JavaScript truthiness, so any non-empty text takes the true branch.
Empty text is still text, so Excel rejects it. JavaScript treats it as falsy.
An error in the condition must propagate. The engine sees a non-empty string, which is truthy, and silently takes the TRUE branch — a wrong ANSWER, not a wrong error.
The error is in the branch that IS taken, so it must surface.

Arguments are evaluated eagerly here, unlike Excel, but the error is produced as a VALUE rather than thrown, so IF can still discard it. The guard idiom survives — see fn-logic-if-guard-divide-by-zero-012.
The standard divide-by-zero guard. Eager evaluation computes 1/0 anyway, but the #DIV/0! is discarded with the untaken branch, so no error leaks.

Below minimum arity. The engine returns the JavaScript value `undefined`, which JSON cannot express, so `actual` is omitted. An undefined cell value is the most damaging arity failure in the engine: it is neither a value nor an error, and everything downstream stringifies it to 'undefined'.
IF takes at most three arguments.

Sheets maps IF over the range, so the anchor cell shows the result for A1 = 0, which is 2. The engine tests the JavaScript array itself, which is always truthy, so ANY range condition takes the true branch regardless of its contents.
IFS returns the value for the FIRST true condition.
Minimum arity is one condition/value pair.
Documented error outcome: no condition is true.
Excel does not surface an error from a value it did not select, and neither does the engine — the error is computed eagerly but then discarded.
An error in a CONDITION must propagate. The engine sees a truthy string and returns the matching value.
Right answer for the wrong reason: the no-match path also returns #N/A, so a missing-argument bug is invisible here.
A trailing condition with no value is an arity error. The engine simply ignores the dangling argument.
Right answer for the wrong reason: the loop needs a pair, finds none, and falls through to the no-match #N/A.
Minimum arity is one.
Any non-zero number is TRUE.
AND flattens a range.
A text argument that is not a logical is rejected. JavaScript truthiness accepts it.
An error argument must propagate. The engine sees a truthy string and reports TRUE, so a divide-by-zero upstream becomes a confident TRUE downstream.
AND ignores blank cells, and with no logical values left it is #VALUE!. The engine resolves the blank to 0 and answers FALSE.
Below minimum arity. Array.every on an empty list is vacuously true, so the engine answers TRUE.
Right answer only in shape: Array.some on an empty list is FALSE, which is not an error but at least is not a false positive.
XOR is TRUE when an ODD number of arguments is TRUE.
Minimum arity is one.
Both texts count as TRUE under JavaScript truthiness, so the engine answers FALSE (two trues) instead of erroring.
Both the bare keyword and the call form are accepted.
TRUE coerces to 1 in arithmetic.
TRUE takes no arguments at all.
Documented error outcome: no match and no default.
A trailing odd argument is the default.
Minimum arity is three.
SWITCH compares text the same way the = operator does, which is case-insensitive. The engine uses JavaScript === and misses the match.
A number does not match the text form of itself.
An error in a result that was not selected is discarded.
The engine returns the JavaScript value `undefined` (args.length 0 is even, so it returns args[-1]), which JSON cannot express; `actual` is omitted.
Right answer for the wrong reason: the no-match path also returns #N/A.
IFERROR catches every error type including #N/A.
The most common real use of IFERROR.
IFERROR does not re-check its fallback.

In Excel the comparison itself is #DIV/0!, so IFERROR catches it. Here the comparison operator coerces the error to 0 with toNum, producing a plain FALSE that IFERROR has nothing to catch. This is the single most dangerous defect in the error model: it makes IFERROR unreliable in exactly the guarded-comparison pattern it exists for.

The argument is a text literal, not an error, so IFERROR must return it unchanged. The engine classifies any string starting with '#' as an error, so ordinary data such as a hash-prefixed ticket id is silently swallowed.
Realistic version of fn-logic-iferror-text-that-looks-like-error-009: any user text beginning with # is treated as an error value.

Google Sheets allows the one-argument form and returns blank on error; Excel requires two arguments. Sheets is used here because it is the only product that produces a cell value. The engine returns the JavaScript value `undefined`, which JSON cannot express, so `actual` is omitted.
The one-argument form with a non-error value passes it through.
Returns `undefined`; `actual` omitted.
IFNA catches only #N/A; every other error passes through.
#N/A produced rather than written as a literal: the tokenizer stops an error scan at '/', so '#N/A' cannot be typed into a formula at all.
IFNA requires two arguments in both products. The engine returns `undefined`; JSON cannot express it, so `actual` is omitted.
Returns `undefined`; `actual` omitted.

The argument is ordinary text that happens to read '#N/A'. Excel returns it unchanged; the engine cannot tell text from an error value and substitutes the fallback. Built by concatenation because the tokenizer cannot lex a '#N/A' literal.
The only way to obtain a #N/A literal in this engine; the tokenizer stops an error scan at '/' so '=#N/A' lexes as '#N'.
#N/A poisons arithmetic.
Concatenation must propagate the error rather than paste its text. The engine pastes.
NA takes no arguments; Sheets reports the arity error as #N/A, which is indistinguishable from NA's own result, so this passes by accident.
An empty cell is blank. The engine resolves an unset or cleared cell to the NUMBER 0, so ISBLANK can never be TRUE for a real cell.
Same defect as fn-logic-isblank-empty-cell-001 for a cell that was never written. ISBLANK is unusable as written.
Empty text is a value, not a blank. This is the mirror image of fn-logic-isblank-empty-cell-001: the engine gets the literal case wrong in the other direction.
A text literal that looks numeric is still text. The engine tests Number(v) instead of the type, so imported text digits are misreported as numbers.
A logical is not a number. Number(true) is 1, so the engine says TRUE.
An empty cell is not a number. The engine resolves it to 0.
The exact complement of fn-logic-isnumber-numeric-text-005; the same coercion bug reports text digits as not-text.
An error is not text. Because the engine models errors as strings, ISTEXT reports TRUE for every error value.
ISERROR includes #N/A; ISERR excludes it.

In Excel a comparison against an error IS an error. Here the comparison operator coerces the error to 0 first, so ISERROR sees a plain FALSE. Every error check placed after a comparison is therefore blind.
Ordinary text that begins with # is not an error. The engine's isErr test is a string prefix check, so real data is misclassified.
The one behaviour that distinguishes ISERR from ISERROR.
#N/A survives arithmetic, so ISNA still sees it.
#N/A produced by a function rather than written as a literal, which the tokenizer cannot lex.
A comparison yields a logical.
Boundary: the sign is ignored.
Excel truncates to 3, which is odd. The engine takes 3.5 % 2 = 1.5, which is neither 0 nor 1, so BOTH ISODD and ISEVEN answer FALSE for the same value.
Non-numeric text is rejected. toNum turns it into 0.
ISODD does not accept a logical.
Boundary: zero is even.
Excel truncates to 2, which is even.
toNum turns unparseable text into 0, so the engine confidently reports 'even'.
The error coerces to 0, which the engine calls even. An error becomes TRUE.
The most common ISBLANK idiom, broken by the unset-cell-is-zero defect.
